articles.title: Daily weather tracker: Bay of Bengal depression intensifies as heavy rain batters Andhra Pradesh, Odisha - Down To Earth

articles.full_text:
Bay of Bengal depression intensifies, threatening heavy to very heavy rainfall across Andhra Pradesh and Odisha with widespread weather disruptions.
IMD issues orange alert for coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha as the system approaches, bringing torrential rain, thunderstorms and strong winds.
Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Chandigarh may witness monsoon withdrawal within two to three days as conditions become increasingly favourable.
Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Maharashtra and northeastern states face heavy rainfall, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds over several areas.
Farmers and fishermen advised caution as heavy rain, waterlogging, rough seas and strong winds pose risks to crops, livestock and livelihoods.
A depression over the west-central and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal is intensifying, raising the prospect of heavy to very heavy rainfall across Andhra Pradesh and Odisha over the next 24 hours. The weather system is also expected to trigger thunderstorms, lightning and strong winds across several states, even as the southwest monsoon begins its accelerated withdrawal from parts of northern India.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast issued on the morning of September 22, 2026, conditions are becoming favourable for the monsoon to retreat from the remaining areas of Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi during the next two to three days. Further withdrawal is also possible from parts of Rajasthan, Saurashtra and Kutch, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and western Uttar Pradesh.
The depression over the Bay of Bengal moved west-northwestwards at around 17 kmph during the previous six hours. The system is expected to strengthen further into a deep depression within the next 12 hours before continuing its west-northwestward movement.
The weather system is forecast to cross the north Andhra Pradesh–south Odisha coast between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur from the night of September 23 to the morning of September 24. Its movement is likely to produce widespread rainfall, gusty winds and thunderstorms across the eastern and central parts of the country.
Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha are expected to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall on Tuesday, with the IMD issuing an orange alert for the affected areas. Rainfall between 115.6 mm to 204.4 mm could occur at isolated locations.
The downpour may lead to waterlogging in low-lying areas, disruption of road traffic and difficult travel conditions. Residents in vulnerable locations have been advised to remain alert and monitor official weather updates, particularly as the depression approaches the coast.
The weather system is also expected to influence conditions in Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Gangetic West Bengal, Karnataka, Konkan and Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, Assam and Meghalaya. These areas have been placed under a yellow alert for heavy rainfall, with isolated locations potentially receiving between 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm of rain.
Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and winds reaching 40 to 50 kmph are possible over Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Gangetic West Bengal, Konkan and Goa, Madhya Maharashtra and Marathwada. Gusty winds and thunderstorms may also affect Gujarat, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Kerala, Lakshadweep and parts of the western Himalayan region.
Rough sea conditions are expected over parts of the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea as the depression strengthens. Strong winds may also affect areas near the southern Myanmar coast and the Gulf of Mannar. Fishermen have been advised to follow warnings issued by the weather department and local authorities and avoid venturing into the sea during hazardous conditions.
The anticipated rainfall could have a significant impact on agricultural operations. Farmers in vulnerable districts have been advised to ensure proper drainage in fields and protect harvested crops, fodder, fertilisers and agricultural equipment from rain and strong winds.
Spraying pesticides or fertilisers during thunderstorms or heavy rainfall should be avoided. Livestock should be moved to secure shelters, particularly during periods of lightning and strong winds.
Despite the developing rain system, unusually high temperatures continue in parts of the country. On September 21, Jaisalmer in Rajasthan recorded the highest maximum temperature at 40.5°C. Haflong in Assam recorded a minimum temperature of 16.5°C among the country's plains.
As the monsoon withdraws from northern India, weather patterns are expected to gradually change. However, local showers and thunderstorms may continue in some areas even after the withdrawal begins.

Odisha gears up as deep depression to bring heavy rain, red alert in 7 districts
With the deep depression expected to bring heavy rain and gusty winds, the Odisha government has reviewed preparedness, readied shelters and personnel, and issued warnings in coastal and southern parts of the state.
Advertisement
Civil defence personnel make announcement at a beach. (PTI/Representational)
The Odisha government said on Monday that it has deployed personnel and machinery at strategic locations to deal with the impact of a deep depression that is likely to hit the state on the night of September 23.
The India Meteorological Department said the weather system over the Bay of Bengal had intensified into a depression and was likely to become a deep depression in the next 24 hours before crossing the coast between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur on the night of September 23. The state has also warned fishermen not to venture into the sea till September 24, while red alerts have been issued for parts of southern Odisha between September 23 and 25.
Chief Secretary Anu Garg reviewed the state's preparedness at a meeting attended by senior officials. Collectors of 11 districts joined the meeting virtually, and Garg directed them to keep cyclone and flood shelters ready to accommodate people if required.
"I have visited several cyclone shelters during the day and overseen arrangements there. The people are being made aware of the impending weather conditions," Ganjam Collector V Keerthi Vasan told reporters.
Collectors of coastal districts, including Puri, Khurda, Jagatsinghpur, Balasore, Bhadrak and Kendrapara, have been using public address systems to advise fishermen not to venture into the sea until September 24. Those already at sea have been asked to return.
According to the IMD, the well-marked low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal intensified into a depression. At 5.30 pm, the system was centred about 310 km southeast of Puri.
Asked whether the system could intensify into a cyclonic storm, Garg said the IMD had forecast it to become a deep depression and not a cyclone. "The government has put the required personnel and machines in place to handle extremely heavy rainfall and gusty winds in the coastal and southern regions of the state," she said.
"In a nutshell, the weather system will bring a lot of rain and comparatively less wind. Therefore, the state is prepared to handle the situation," she added.
IMD Bhubaneswar centre director Manorama Mohanty said rainfall had started in different parts of the state and was likely to continue until September 25. A red alert has been issued for parts of southern Odisha for September 23-25. Heavy to very heavy rainfall, with extremely heavy rain at isolated places, is likely in Koraput, Gajapati and Ganjam on September 23-24.
Kalahandi, Nabarangpur, Koraput and Malkangiri have also been issued red alerts for September 24-25. The IMD said squally winds with speeds of 55-65 kmph, gusting to 75 kmph, are likely along and off the south Odisha-north Andhra Pradesh coasts from the morning of September 23 to the evening of September 24.

articles.full_text:
The Odisha government has put coastal and southern districts on high alert following the formation of a depression over the West Central and adjoining Northwest Bay of Bengal.
Moving west-northwestwards at a speed of 18 km/h, the system is expected to intensify into a deep depression over the next 12 hours before making landfall between Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and Gopalpur (Odisha) between the night of September 23 and early morning of September 24.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast widespread light-to-moderate rain across the state, with extremely heavy rainfall expected in isolated parts of southern Odisha over the next few days.
Severe Weather Forecast & District Warnings
The IMD has issued phased Red Warnings for the hardest-hit regions:
September 23–24: Red Warning for Koraput, Gajapati, and Ganjam, where extremely heavy rainfall is anticipated.
September 24–25: Red Warning shifts to Kalahandi, Nabarangpur, Koraput, and Malkangiri.
Along the south Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh coasts, wind speeds are currently hovering between 40 and 50 km/h, with gusts reaching 60 km/h. Wind speeds are expected to pick up further, reaching 55 to 65 km/h with gusts up to 75 km/h by September 23–24.
Fishermen have been strictly advised not to venture into the Westcentral, Northwest, and Southwest Bay of Bengal or along the Odisha-Andhra Pradesh-West Bengal coastline until September 24 due to rough sea conditions.
State Preparation & Response Efforts
In anticipation of the storm, Odisha Chief Secretary reviewed state preparedness with key departments, including the Special Relief Commissioner (SRC), Fire Services, Health, Police, and District Collectors of southern districts.
Special attention is being paid to landslide-prone regions in Gajapati, Rayagada, Ganjam, Koraput, and Malkangiri.
Key Disaster Management Steps Undertaken:
ODRAF Deployment: A total of 33 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) teams have been mobilised. 24 teams are already deployed across vulnerable districts (Ganjam: 6, Koraput: 6, Gajapati: 3, Malkangiri: 3, Rayagada: 3, Kalahandi: 2, and Balangir: 1), while 9 teams remain on standby at Chhatrapur.
River & Dam Monitoring: Major southern rivers—including the Rushikulya and Vamsadhara—are currently flowing below danger levels. Reservoir capacities remain stable, with Upper Indravati at 83.6% and Upper Kolab at 54.5%.
Health & Safety Shelters: Local administrations have been instructed to prepare cyclone and flood shelters, stock essential medical supplies, and maintain high operational readiness.
Advisory for the Public
The state government has advised citizens to remain vigilant, avoid waterlogged or low-lying areas, and strictly follow updates issued by local administration and the IMD. Senior officials remain stationed at headquarters to monitor the evolving situation closely.
